title: Origin raises $20M to scale autonomous construction robots
key_facts: Origin, a San Francisco robotics company, has emerged from stealth with $20 million in funding, co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures, according to Origin.
Its OG-1 robot autonomously does drywall finishing: applying compound, sanding and priming, at heights up to 14 feet.
Pilots are planned with two large US drywall contractors, with more work scheduled in Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia.
Origin targets 150 deployed robots by the end of 2027.
The company says its robots work at three times human speed with human-level finishing quality, based on its own deployments.
Human crews still handle site mapping and material replenishment.
quote_evidence: Origin has emerged from stealth with $20 million in funding to expand deployment of its OG-1 robot, which autonomously performs drywall finishing work on construction sites.
Origin also said its robots are working at three times human speed while maintaining human-level finishing quality, based on its own deployments.
Origin plans to expand OG-1 into areas including taping, drywall installation, drilling and conduit installation while targeting 150 deployed robots by the end of 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Targets a labour shortage in skilled interior construction work.
notes: Company claims relayed by AI Insider.
